assumptions: the vendor prefill path is rewritten to chunk the sequence, so the expert weights are read once per layer rather than once per chunk
the indexer einsum sustains the best rate measured above
compute and weight streaming do not overlap, so the sum is a lower bound on wall time rather than an estimate of it
derived.empirical_prefill_note: the measured 8,000-token prefill (47.7 s), which already contains one full weight sweep and every per-layer overhead, plus the derived growth of the O(S^2) indexer term. It excludes the O(S^2) growth of sparse attention, so it is an estimate of the right order, not a bound.
derived.weight_sweep_seconds_note: at the conservative 4.04 GiB/s first-touch rate

expert_sweep_one_layer.note: this rate depends entirely on the page cache. 4.04 GiB/s is the first-touch rate measured on an untouched layer before any model ran; the rate recorded here is whatever the cache state happened to be, and is the optimistic end. The conservative figure below uses 4.04.
